correctness.rationale: For \(A=(-1,0)\), \(B=(1,0)\), \(C=(0,2)\), and \(P=(0,y)\) with \(0<y<2\), direct orthogonal projection gives the three pedal vertices and hence \(R_p=(1+y^2)/(1+2y)\) and the stated closed formula for \(r_p\). The ambient circumradius is \(R=5/4\). At \(y=1/100\), substituting the exact formulas reduces the claimed reversal to an inequality involving \(\sqrt2\) and \(\sqrt{50005}\); the rational lower bounds \(\sqrt2>140/99\) and \(\sqrt{50005}>1118/5\) certify it exactly. Moreover the defect tends as \(y\downarrow0\) to \(-1/4+(4/5)(\sqrt{10}-2\sqrt2)>0\); continuity therefore gives an open interior boundary layer of counterexamples, not a single numerical accident.
residual_risks: The verifier supplies symbolic/numeric checks only; the exact coordinate derivation and rational radical bounds establish the claim.
